forces: Admission must be gated by an explicit bounded capacity so unbounded concurrent submission cannot cause unbounded resource use, without depending on any transport, queue, or storage runtime mechanism.
Overload must be a deterministic, immediate, synchronous outcome — never queued, never a silent drop — so a caller can rely on the result of one submit call.

Capacity accounting must never drift regardless of whether the wrapped operation succeeds or fails, and must remain correct under concurrent submission with only cooperative (non-preemptive) scheduling.
The gate must compose above any delivery mechanism (a raw handoff, a retry-wrapped delivery, or otherwise) without coupling to any one of their result shapes.

candidate_approaches.summary: A generic synchronous admission gate that wraps any async operation, incrementing/decrementing an in-flight counter with no locks, rejecting immediately at capacity.

approach-alternative-implement-delivery-.reason: A buffering queue reintroduces exactly the unbounded-memory risk backpressure exists to prevent, contradicts the issue's explicit exclusion of queue capacity beyond the bound, and turns a deterministic immediate result into a delayed one the caller cannot rely on synchronously.

concurrent-admission test: exactly `capacity` submissions proceed and every submission beyond that is rejected
